case_title: BALU SUDAM KHALDE & ANR. v. THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
aggravating_circumstances: Use of dangerous weapons, multiple blows, victim was unarmed and helpless
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s. 302 r/w 34, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were strangers who engaged in a verbal altercation that escalated into a physical fight. The accused used dangerous weapons, including a sickle and sword, to assault the victim. The victim sustained severe injuries, including bleeding on his head, left paw, wrist, right hand, and right shoulder, and ultimately succumbed to his injuries. The victim was taken to a hospital where he was declared dead. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovery of weapons. The trial court convicted the accused of murder under Section 302 of the IPC, and the High Court upheld the conviction. The accused claimed the case fell under Exception 4 to Section 300, but the Supreme Court rejected this, emphasizing the use of dangerous weapons and the victim's helplessness.
